PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Easier fault localization and readability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for a single Arrange-Act-Assert and a single method call under test. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct Act operations -> only pilha0.desempilha(); (2) Name does not indicate multiple operations; (3) Single assertion group (try-act-assert via fail/verifyException). VERDICT: compliant because the test performs one operation (desempilha) and asserts the expected exception in a single Arrange-Act-Assert flow.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be independent. RATIONALE: Independent tests can run in any order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Before/@After or use of only local variables. DECISION RULES: (1) No @Before/@After present but (4) tests use only local variables. VERDICT: compliant because the test constructs and uses a local Pilha instance without shared mutable state.

DECISION RULES: (1) Count test methods -> only one test in the class; (2) All tests are not covering both flows. VERDICT: non-compliant because the class contains only a single test that verifies the exceptional path (pop from empty) and lacks a corresponding happy-path test that verifies normal push/pop behavior.

DECISION RULES: (1) The test exercises an empty stack (a boundary). VERDICT: compliant because popping an empty stack is an explicit boundary case.
